# Incident Report — MTA 2024-08-15 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## 1. Scope of Evidence
Single evidence file reviewed: `2024-08-15-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (18,189 packets, capture window 2024-08-15 04:09:43 – 04:42:26 local capture time). No IDS/Suricata alert export was present in the evidence directory — only the pcap. All findings below are derived directly from packet analysis with `tshark`.

## 2. Victim Host

| Attribute | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.8.15.133** | DHCP lease (frames 1–6) |
| MAC address | **00:1c:bf:03:54:82** (Intel Corporate) | DHCP client, ARP, Ethernet headers |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-H8ALZBV** | DHCP Option 12, NBNS name registration |
| Windows/AD domain | **LAFONTAINEBLEU.ORG** (NetBIOS: LAFONTAINEBLEU) | Kerberos realm, LDAP base DN, DNS SRV lookups |
| Logged-in domain user | **plucero** (display name "Pierce Lucero", CN=Pierce Lucero,CN=Users,DC=lafontainebleu,DC=org) | Kerberos AS-REQ/TGS-REQ CNames, LDAP query |
| Domain controller | 10.8.15.4 (WIN-JEGJIX7Q9RS.lafontainebleu.org) | DHCP server / Kerberos / LDAP responses |

## 3. Malware Family
**Latrodectus** (JS-downloader → BITS-delivered DLL loader → HTTP C2). 

**Attribution basis: behavioral/TTP, not signature-confirmed.** No Suricata/IDS ruleset was supplied with this evidence, so no signature hit exists to cite. The call is based on matching a well-documented Latrodectus infection chain observed directly in the traffic:

1. Fake "verify you are human" (ClickFix-style) FedEx-themed lure page reached over Cloudflare-fronted domains `checkfedexexp.com`.
2. Delivery of a ZIP containing a single, deliberately bloated (~6.99 MB, mostly padded with unrelated book/report text) `.js` file named to look like an invoice.
3. The JS contains a `WScript.Sleep(10000)` anti-sandbox delay and a hard-coded callback URL, consistent with a JScript downloader stage.
4. The host then issued a Microsoft BITS job (`User-Agent: Microsoft BITS/7.8`, a common LOLBin abuse technique) to fetch a Windows PE32+ DLL from a bare-IP HTTP server.
5. That DLL's internal name is `release.dll`, exporting `DllRegisterServer`/`DllRegisterServerEx` — i.e., built to be launched via `regsvr32.exe`.
6. Immediately after, the host began a persistent HTTP beacon (repeating every ~5–20 seconds, continuing through the end of the capture) to the same bare IP using `GET /` and `POST /` requests carrying an encrypted blob in a `Cookie:` header and a distinctive malformed user-agent string `Mozilla / 5.0 (compatible; MSIE 6.0; Windows NT 5.1; SV1; .NET CLR 1.0.3705)` (note the stray space after "Mozilla").

This chain — fake-CAPTCHA lure → oversized padded JS → BITS-fetched regsvr32-loadable DLL → encrypted Cookie-based HTTP/80 beacon with that specific spaced MSIE6 UA — is the recognized fingerprint of Latrodectus loader campaigns. Because no Suricata/YARA output accompanied the capture, treat this as high-confidence behavioral attribution, not a signature match.

## 4. Timeline (all times in capture-local timezone, 2024-08-15)

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 04:09:43 | Capture starts; host DHCP-leases 10.8.15.133 |
| 04:10:58.485 | DNS resolves `quote.checkfedexexp.com` → 104.21.55.70 / 172.67.170.159 (Cloudflare) |
| 04:10:58.536 | `GET http://quote.checkfedexexp.com/managements?...` returns a 2.77 MB ZIP (`application/octet-stream`) containing the JS downloader |
| 04:11:24.025 | DNS resolves `business.checkfedexexp.com` → 172.67.170.159 / 104.21.55.70; JS beacons to `https://business.checkfedexexp.com/data-privacy?...` |
| 04:11:58.562 | First contact to C2 IP **72.5.43.29** — BITS `HEAD`/`GET /data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` |
| 04:12:00 onward | Sustained `GET /` and `POST /` beacon traffic to **72.5.43.29:80**, continuing to end of capture (04:42:26) |

## 5. Indicators of Compromise

### Command-and-control endpoints
- **72.5.43.29:80** — HTTP C2, `GET /` and `POST /` beacon with encrypted `Cookie:` header, UA `Mozilla / 5.0 (compatible; MSIE 6.0; Windows NT 5.1; SV1; .NET CLR 1.0.3705)`. Repeated dozens of times over ~30 minutes.

### Malicious domains
- `quote.checkfedexexp.com` (resolved 104.21.55.70, 172.67.170.159)
- `business.checkfedexexp.com` (resolved 172.67.170.159, 104.21.55.70)

### Malicious URLs
- `http://quote.checkfedexexp.com/managements?16553a25e45250a41fd5&endeds=MIGpq&JStx=59bf050d37df88a9-ade43358-eaa1220b-0571422b-0f33e6aa150e86bafd0ed4&Ld=9d7502d88d752a27b1d00587309184b5a215` — delivered the ZIP/JS downloader
- `https://business.checkfedexexp.com/data-privacy?zj=ZzqRKxVRQ&pOd=GEokiOXFwH&sourcedp=tQMQJlIo&Tfocontent...` — embedded callback URL found inside the JS payload
- `http://72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` — BITS-fetched DLL payload

### Transferred files and hashes

| File | Size | SHA256 | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `managements` (server-side path, delivered as ZIP) | 2,767,804 bytes | `798563fcf7600f7ef1a35996291a9dfb5f9902733404dd499e2e736ea1dc6fc5` | ZIP archive from quote.checkfedexexp.com |
| `Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js` | 6,990,020 bytes | `dab98819d1d7677a60f5d06be210d45b74ae5fd8cf0c24ec1b3766e25ce6dc2c` | Contained inside the ZIP; padded JScript downloader with `WScript.Sleep` anti-sandbox delay |
| `0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` | 159,232 bytes | `b7aec5f73d2a6bbd8cd920edb4760e2edadc98c3a45bf4fa994d47ca9cbd02f6` (MD5 `59b7b8d29252a9128536fbd08d24375f`) | PE32+ DLL, x86-64, internal module name `release.dll`, exports `DllRegisterServer`/`DllRegisterServerEx` (regsvr32-loadable). Fetched from C2 via abused BITS job. |

### Not IOCs (verified benign, ruled out during analysis)
Traffic to `msedge.b.tlu.dl.delivery.mp.microsoft.com` (199.232.210.172) and `acroipm2.adobe.com` was legitimate Windows Update Delivery Optimization and Adobe ARM update-check traffic respectively — unrelated to the intrusion, despite superficially resembling the malicious BITS activity.

## 6. Recommended Actions
- Isolate DESKTOP-H8ALZBV (10.8.15.133) from the network immediately; treat the `plucero` domain account as compromised (force credential reset, review for lateral AD activity from that account/host).
- Block/sinkhole `72.5.43.29`, `quote.checkfedexexp.com`, `business.checkfedexexp.com` at the perimeter.
- Hunt endpoint telemetry for: `regsvr32.exe` loading `release.dll`, a `bitsadmin`/BITS job created shortly after JS execution, and `wscript.exe` executing a file named `Invoice-*.js`.
- Full forensic imaging of the host is warranted before remediation, since sustained C2 beaconing continued through the end of the capture with no evidence collection of what commands/tasking the operator sent.
